title: Throw something back, get pushed forward

predict.q: You're standing still on a skateboard, holding a heavy ball. You throw it hard, straight backwards. What happens to you?
options: Nothing: there's nothing behind you to push against
You roll backwards, after the ball
predict.reveal: You roll forwards. Many people expect nothing to happen because there's no wall behind you, but the ball itself is what you push against: shove it back and it shoves you forward.

interactive.brief: The one thing you should see is the skater rolling forwards faster when you throw a heavier ball or throw it harder.
interactive.title: Throw a ball off a skateboard

controls.label: How fast you throw it backwards

interactive.whatAmILookingAt: The push on the ball and the push on you are equal and opposite, so the 'oomph' (mass × speed) the ball gets backwards equals the oomph you get forwards. Your speed = ball's mass × throw speed ÷ your mass. In symbols: v = m × u ÷ M, with M = 70 kg for you and the board.
interactive.ignores: Friction in the wheels, air resistance, and a small correction for the fact that you start rolling while you are still throwing.

numbers.label: Your speed forwards at the start (m/s)

explain.text:
When you threw the ball, you rolled the other way, and a heavier ball or a harder throw sent you off faster.

Here's why. To get the ball moving backwards, your arms have to push on it. And a push never comes alone: the ball pushes back on you, just as hard, in the opposite direction. That's [[Newton's third law]]: for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.[^1]

Notice what you didn't need: no wall, nothing behind you to push against. The thing you pushed on was the ball you threw.

A jet engine plays exactly this trick, with air instead of a ball. It grabs air and flings it out of the back, and the air shoves the engine, and the plane bolted to it, forwards.[^2] That forward shove is called [[thrust]].

So the secret of a jet engine isn't pushing against the sky. **It's throwing something backwards.**

analogy.text: It's like the kick of a garden hose: turn the tap up and the nozzle pushes back into your hand, because water is being thrown out of the front of it.
analogy.breaks: The hose's water arrives already pushed along by the mains. A jet engine has to grab still air and speed it up itself, and that's what the fuel is for.

say.prompt: In your own words: how can a jet engine push a plane forwards when there's nothing solid behind it to push against?
rubric: It throws air (or gas) out of the back
That air pushes back on the engine, just as hard, forwards
Nothing solid is needed: the thrown air is what it pushes on
say.model: The engine throws air out of its back. Pushing that air backwards means the air pushes the engine forwards just as hard, so the plane moves. It doesn't need a wall or the ground: the air it throws is the thing it pushes against.

checks.q: A rocket fires its engine in deep space, where there is no air at all. What happens?
options: Nothing: with no air outside, there's nothing to push against
It speeds up: the gas it throws back pushes it forwards
It only moves if it's near a planet it can push off
It drifts backwards, following its own exhaust

misconception.0: Thinks the push comes from the air outside. It comes from the gas the rocket throws out, so no outside air is needed.
misconception.2: Thinks an engine must push off something solid. A rocket pushes on its own exhaust, wherever it is.
misconception.3: Thinks the thrower follows what it throws. Throwing something backwards pushes you the opposite way.

checks.why: A rocket carries everything it burns and throws the hot gas out of the back, and that gas pushes the rocket forwards. It needs no air outside to push against.

checks.q: Keep the throw at 10 m/s. Choose a ball heavy enough that you roll away at 1 m/s.
checks.why: Your speed is ball mass × throw speed ÷ 70 kg. At 10 m/s you need a 7 kg ball: 7 × 10 ÷ 70 = 1 m/s.

checks.q: Which of these moves forwards in the same way a jet engine does?
options: A squid squirting water out behind it to dart away
A sailing boat being pushed along by the wind
A car whose tyres grip and push on the road

misconception.1: The wind pushes the boat from outside; the boat throws nothing backwards.
misconception.2: Tyres push on the ground, the very thing a jet engine doesn't need.

checks.why: A squid throws water backwards and the water pushes it forwards: a push from what it throws, just like a jet engine with air.

sources.title: Newton's Third Law of Motion — NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.quote: for every action (force) in nature there is an equal and opposite reaction

sources.title: How Does a Jet Engine Work? — NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.quote: As the jets of gas shoot backward, the engine and the aircraft are thrust forward.
